title: Stripe-oriented KV shuffle and BW amplification notes
linked_artifacts: confluence:KV stripe experiment notes - page id 987654321
body:
Purpose:
We observed intermittent spikes in GPU memory channel utilization and unexpected read amplification on long-tail requests. This note captures an exploratory set of microbenchmarks and field traces that investigate an architectural pattern we call "stripe-oriented KV shuffling": when model KV entries get redistributed (due to eviction, compaction, or multi-request interleaving) across memory channels (stripes), reuse locality degrades and memory-bandwidth amplification occurs.

Hypothesis:
1) When hot keys are scattered across many stripes (channels), the effective reuse rate per channel drops and per-channel DMA bursts become smaller but more frequent, increasing bus contention and latency variability.
2) Occasional rebalancing (repack or eviction-driven shuffle) creates short-lived periods of high cross-channel traffic that amplify bandwidth by 1.1–2.0x relative to steady-state.
3) Simple, channel-aware residency steering (preferentially placing related KV pages on same stripe) can reduce amplification while keeping eviction efficiency.

Experimental setup (hardware & workloads):
- Hardware: 2x A100 GPUs (40GB), NVLink disabled for these runs to amplify PCIe channel effects, host CPU: 64-core Cascade Lake, DDR4-3200, OS kernel 5.15.
- Memory profiler: per-channel counters from vendor perf driver + PCIe counters sampled at 1ms resolution.
- Runtime: in-process serving binary from branch stripe-experiments (PR 812).
- Workloads: synthetic mix to stress KV: (a) Zipfian-Theta=0.8 read-heavy traffic with 10k distinct keys; (b) mixed read/write trace from production-sampled chat sessions skewed to 3k hot keys; (c) adversarial shuffle trace where request sequence reorders keys to encourage cross-stripe footprints.
- Key -> page mapping: baseline (round-robin stripe assignment), stripe-width variable (1..8 pages per stripe group).
- Metrics captured per experiment: overall reuse rate (fraction of hits served from resident KV without page fault), per-channel bandwidth (MB/s), cross-channel concurrent DMA bursts (counts per second), p50/p95/p99 tail LMs for token generation latency, eviction churn (pages/sec), and page movement events.
